newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: C&W takes BT, MCI merger in stride - CEO.
newsitem.headline: C&W takes BT, MCI merger in stride - CEO.

text.p: Richard Brown, chief executive of Cable and Wireless said on Sunday he was happy with the course the British telecommunication firm has taken and took in stride the merger of British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp.

"We are happy with the course of actions we are on the way with. There are mergers appearing all over...This is one more. How well it works, with all the regulatory debates, remains to be seen," Brown told Reuters at an interview.
Brown, who was in Singapore to open Cable and Wireless new office on Monday, took the news in stride when informed the merger.
"We think we have a great business in Cable and Wireless. We are big enough to be successful and independent. We are global and small enough to be nimble in the market place."
"I think the winners of the future will not be the bigger players but the better players."

On Sunday, British Telecommunications Plc (BT) unveiled the largest merger in British corporate history, linking up with the number two U.S. long distance phone company, MCI Communications Corp. The deal has yet to be agreed by regulatory authorities on either sides of the Atlantic.

BT, whose attempts to merge with British rival Cable and wireless failed six months ago, said the deal would create a world leading communications power house with an annual revenue of over 25 billion pounds ($41 billion), cash flow of about 7.5 billion pounds and 43 million business and residential customers in 70 countries.

Cable and Wireless is one of the world's leading providers of international telecommunications services, providing mobile communications in 30 countries and operates the world's largest, most advanced cableship fleet.
